title: Norovirus Outbreaks Fell by More Than Half This Season, and CDC Says the Current Total Is Typical - Medical Daily

analysis.time: Publication date: July 28, 2026. Event period: August 1, 2025 to May 7, 2026 (norovirus season).
analysis.location_and_population: United States, reported by state health departments participating in CDC's NoroSTAT network.
analysis.event: Confirmed norovirus outbreak data showing a 53% decrease in outbreaks (1,194 in 2025-2026 vs. 2,534 in 2024-2025), described by CDC as within the typical range for seasonal years 2012-2025.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 1,194 reported outbreaks in the 2025-2026 season, representing a decline from the previous season but still within the middle 50% (interquartile range) of historical data. No explicit risk level stated.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC's NoroSTAT surveillance system monitors outbreaks; full-season data expected after July 31, 2026. Prevention advice remains unchanged regardless of outbreak count.

analysis.brief_en: The CDC reports a significant 53% drop in norovirus outbreaks for the 2025-2026 season, with 1,194 cases compared to 2,534 the previous year. However, officials emphasize this season's total falls within the typical range observed over the past decade, marking it as ordinary rather than exceptional. The NoroSTAT surveillance network, which tracks outbreaks across participating U.S. states, will provide a complete seasonal update by late July. Despite the decrease, health authorities maintain that standard prevention measures remain critical, as even a typical season involves thousands of outbreaks nationwide.

title: Lindblad's National Geographic Sea Bird reported 4th Norovirus outbreak in Alaska - CruiseMapper

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-25. Event dates: July 10th–15th voyage and July 15th–20th voyage, with previous outbreaks in late May and late June.
analysis.location_and_population: Country: United States. Region: Southeast Alaska. Facility: National Geographic Sea Bird cruise ship. Affected population: Passengers and crew members during two voyages.
analysis.event: Confirmed norovirus outbreaks on the National Geographic Sea Bird cruise ship. The CDC reported the third and fourth outbreaks since late May, with laboratory confirmation for the first two outbreaks. The most recent outbreaks occurred during July 10th–15th and July 15th–20th voyages.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Cases: 32 passengers and crew affected across two voyages (19 during July 10th–15th, 13 during July 15th–20th). Symptoms included vomiting, abdominal cramps, and diarrhoea. The CDC has not yet identified the cause of the latest outbreaks. The vessel's scheduled return to Juneau on July 25th was cancelled.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CDC is investigating the outbreaks. Laboratory testing previously confirmed norovirus as the cause of the first two outbreaks. The cause of the latest outbreaks is yet to be determined. The ship's call to Juneau on July 25th was cancelled.

analysis.brief_en: The National Geographic Sea Bird cruise ship, operated by Lindblad Expeditions, has experienced its third and fourth norovirus outbreaks in Southeast Alaska during July 2026. During the July 10th–15th voyage, 19 of 88 passengers and crew fell ill, with 18 passengers and one crew member affected. Symptoms included vomiting and abdominal cramps. In the subsequent July 15th–20th voyage, 13 of 83 passengers and crew reported illness, experiencing diarrhoea, vomiting, and abdominal cramps. In total, 32 passengers and crew were affected across both voyages. While the CDC has not yet identified the cause of these latest outbreaks, laboratory testing previously confirmed norovirus as the cause of two earlier incidents in late May and late June. The vessel's scheduled return to Juneau on July 25th was cancelled.

In the subsequent July 15th–20th voyage, 13 of 83 passengers and crew reported illness, experiencing diarrhoea, vomiting, and abdominal cramps. In total, 32 passengers and crew were affected across both voyages. While the CDC has not yet identified the cause of these latest outbreaks, laboratory testing previously confirmed norovirus as the cause of two earlier incidents in late May and late June. title: 13 people sick in fourth cruise ship GI outbreak in less than 2 months - Yahoo Lifestyle Canada

analysis.time: Publication date: 2026-07-27. Event date: July 15 voyage.
analysis.location_and_population: National Geographic Sea Bird cruise ship operating in Alaska. Affected: 8 of 57 guests and 5 crew members.
analysis.event: Confirmed gastrointestinal illness outbreak on National Geographic Sea Bird, marking the vessel's fourth outbreak in less than two months. Symptoms: abdominal cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 13 total cases (8 guests, 5 crew). The ship has experienced three previous outbreaks since late May, two confirmed as norovirus, one unknown cause. CDC notes 90% of cruise GI outbreaks with confirmed cause are norovirus.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: Cruise company implemented heightened disinfection, cleaning measures, and isolated sick guests and employees. Three voyages (July 20, 25, 30) canceled for enhanced sanitation protocols. Company providing refunds and alternative arrangements to affected guests. Investigation ongoing; cause of current outbreak unknown.

analysis.brief_en: A National Geographic-Lindblad Expeditions cruise ship, National Geographic Sea Bird, reported its fourth gastrointestinal illness outbreak in less than two months during its July 15 voyage in Alaska. Eight of 57 guests and five crew members fell ill with symptoms including abdominal cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea. The cause remains unknown, though previous outbreaks on the same vessel included two norovirus cases and one with an undetermined cause. The cruise company responded by implementing enhanced sanitation protocols, canceling three upcoming voyages, and providing refunds and alternative travel arrangements to affected passengers. The CDC continues to monitor the situation, noting that norovirus is the most common cause of cruise ship GI outbreaks.
analysis.summary_en: A National Geographic-Lindblad Expeditions cruise ship, National Geographic Sea Bird, reported its fourth gastrointestinal illness outbreak in less than two months during its July 15 voyage in Alaska. Eight of 57 guests and five crew members fell ill with symptoms including abdominal cramps, vomiting, and diarrhea. The cause remains unknown, though previous outbreaks on the same vessel included two norovirus cases and one with an undetermined cause. The cruise company responded by implementing enhanced sanitation protocols, canceling three upcoming voyages, and providing refunds and alternative travel arrangements to affected passengers. The CDC continues to monitor the situation, noting that norovirus is the most common cause of cruise ship GI outbreaks.
